title: How Sam Bankman-Fried Actually Lost $8 Billion
hook: By twenty-nine he was worth twenty-six billion dollars. Within a week it was gone, along with eight billion dollars of other people's money -- and the backers who studied his firm for months never once found the hole.
body:
Sam Bankman-Fried graduated MIT in 2014 with a degree in physics and took a trading job at Jane Street Capital in New York. In 2017 he left to found Alameda Research, a crypto trading firm, out of an apartment in Berkeley. In 2019 he co-founded the crypto exchange FTX with MIT classmate Gary Wang, later headquartered in the Bahamas; Caroline Ellison, another Jane Street alum, took over running Alameda, and Nishad Singh joined as director of engineering. A January 2022 funding round valued FTX at $32 billion, with Forbes estimating Bankman-Fried's own net worth at as much as $26 billion. At Bankman-Fried's direction, FTX co-founder Gary Wang built a hidden exception into the exchange's code that let Alameda run a negative balance -- reported at roughly $65 billion of capacity -- that no other account was permitted to carry. Roughly $10 billion in user deposits moved from FTX to Alameda through that exception, propped up in part by FTT, a token FTX had created itself. On November 2, 2022, CoinDesk published a leaked Alameda balance sheet showing billions of its assets sat in that same FTX-printed token. On November 6, Binance CEO Changpeng "CZ" Zhao announced Binance would liquidate its FTT holdings, citing "recent revelations," triggering a bank run; FTX halted withdrawals on November 8, and a proposed Binance acquisition collapsed within a day after a look at FTX's books. On November 11, 2022, FTX, Alameda, and roughly 130 affiliated companies filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in Delaware; Bankman-Fried resigned as CEO, and John J. Ray III, who had overseen the Enron liquidation, was installed to run the wind-down. Bankman-Fried was arrested in Nassau, the Bahamas, on December 12, 2022, the night before he was scheduled to testify before Congress; the DOJ unsealed an eight-count indictment the next day. Gary Wang and Caroline Ellison pleaded guilty in December 2022 and agreed to cooperate with prosecutors; Nishad Singh later pleaded guilty as well. At trial in the Southern District of New York, Ellison testified that Bankman-Fried directed her to use customer funds to cover Alameda's losses, fund investments, buy property, and pay for political donations. On November 2, 2023, a jury convicted Bankman-Fried on all seven counts he faced. On March 28, 2024, Judge Lewis Kaplan sentenced him to 25 years in federal prison and ordered $11 billion in forfeiture. Caroline Ellison was sentenced on September 24, 2024, to 2 years, credited for what the judge called "very, very substantial" cooperation. This is what the SEC and DOJ's own filings, trial testimony, and contemporaneous CoinDesk, CNBC, CNN, NPR and Axios reporting say happened.
